title: Free AI 3D generators for commercial use — or just wait it out?
author: flaxRabbittt
selftext:
Solo hobbyist dev here, working on a 3D tactical RPG in Godot with Claude + MCP. I've been generating characters and props with free accounts on Hunyuan3D and Tripo, then found out their free tiers don't allow commercial use. Meshy's free tier is CC BY 4.0, but credits and downloads are very limited.

Options I'm weighing:

1. Another free, cloud-based generator (no strong local GPU) whose free output can be used commercially, even with attribution.
2. MPFB2 (MakeHuman for Blender, CC0 assets) for humans, plus custom clothing. That means a lot more work on outfits and fitting.
3. Keep using the free tiers as placeholders and replace everything near release. The game will take a few more years, and I'm hoping free commercial options will exist by then (or I pay for one month of a paid plan and regenerate in bulk).

Has anyone gone with option 3? Is it a reasonable bet, or does swapping assets late cause more pain than it's worth (re-rigging, re-splitting meshes for dismemberment, matching scale and style)?

comments.author: JoeEnderman
comments.body:
I'm waiting it out and working on games that don't need 3D assets for the time being but I am sure there's multiple realistic options out there. 

Edit: Since I said there are options, here's the main one. TRELLIS.2 from Microsoft is MIT licensed, so whatever you generate is yours to sell. The restriction you ran into comes from the hosted sites' free tiers, not the models. You can run it on a free Hugging Face Space or rent a 24GB GPU for an hour and batch everything. If you stick with placeholders, lock down your skeleton, scale and dismemberment splits now so swapping later is just busywork.

replies.author: flaxRabbittt
replies.body: Hi thank you. I actually tried TRELLIS.2 on the free HF space some time ago. It's great that it's MIT, but I didn't obtain decent quality: blurry texture, few detailed features, slightly warped shapes. So, I'll try again a bit to see if I find some workaround (like subdividing the target into parts), but I'm probably going with the "wait it out" approach. And also thank you for your other suggestions, those are something I'll follow for sure.

comments.author: Eagle771
comments.body: Hunyuan ai by tencents give you 5 a day

replies.author: flaxRabbittt
replies.body: Hi, thank you but I already use that free service, my issue was the license and, as far as I know, that site is for personal/research use only.

comments.author: OkVariety8064
comments.body:
Meshy or the likes cannot claim copyright over or put limits on use of generated assets, because [AI generated stuff is by default public domain](https://library.osu.edu/site/copyright/2026/02/06/artificial-intelligence-and-the-public-domain/).

> To receive copyright protection in the United States, a work must contain human authorship, among other requirements. The outputs of generative AI can be protected by copyright only where a human author has determined sufficient expressive elements. If a human adds creative elements to the AI-created output, such as arrangements or modifications, then they may be able to claim copyright in their contributions

Legally, you can use any AI generated content without restrictions, regardless of what the providers say. Of course, you will be breaking their terms of service, so they might ban your account, but there's plenty of these service providers anyway.

replies.author: flaxRabbittt
replies.body: Hi, the article is interesting and I understand the reasoning behind the idea, but I'd rather not ship a game built on assets whose terms I knowingly broke. Also, if I'm not wrong, Steam asks you to disclose AI content and confirm you have the rights; this seems a bit too risky to me. Still, good to know that the legal landscape seems less locked down than the providers suggest.

comments.author: Sith_Lord_Aries
comments.body:
Ive run into this same issue.  Trying to run local on my 1080 ti still doesn't give good results and I
 haven't got the gumption to try my hand at 100+ 3d models in blender with no personal experience doing that already

comments.author: EtadanikM
comments.body:
If it's really a few years before it launches, then wait it out. Models will become better. The assets you're paying $100 for today will not be what you pay $100 for in a few years. 

Honestly though, I wouldn't even plan for what happens in a few years. There's at least a 50% chance the gaming industry will be completely disrupted by AI game development by then and your calibration for what you want changes.
